text: 巴西一所高级别生物实验室病毒样本被盗，疑为该校病毒学家窃取
发生了一起生物安全三级（BSL-3）实验室病毒样本失窃案。今年2月，该校病毒学与应用生物技术实验室的一名研究人员发现有几个病毒样本缺失，随即上报校方并向联邦警察报案。校方在内部调查中调取了监控录像。录像显示，该实验室在读博士生迈克尔·爱德华·米勒（Michael Edward Miller）曾在深夜或清晨等异常时段进出实验室并携带物品。
基孔肯雅病毒、登革热病毒及EB病毒（又称人类疱疹病毒4型）。该实验室正是迈克尔的妻子、病毒学家索莱达·帕拉梅塔·米勒（Soledad Palameta Miller）的工作场所。
screen_text.summary: I am XXX an article on my phone about a BSL-3 laboratory virus sample theft in Brazil involving a researcher and his wife.

screen_text.label: Phone screen scrolling down
text: 基孔肯雅病毒、登革热病毒及EB病毒（又称人类疱疹病毒4型）。该实验室正是迈克尔的妻子、病毒学家索莱达·帕拉梅塔·米勒（Soledad Palameta Miller）的工作场所。3月23日，警方正式逮捕索莱达，认定她涉嫌窃取病毒样本并试图销毁证据。
此次“内部泄露”事件在巴西病毒学界引发了强烈反应，因为 BSL-3 实验室通常具有极为严格的准入机制和样本管理制度。

text_visible: Given a data element x and neural net f_theta(x, t), implement the following diffusion training steps:
1. Sample the diffusion timestep t ~ Uniform(0, 1)
2. Compute the noise strength following a cosine schedule: alpha_t = cos(pi/2 * t), sigma_t = sin(pi/2 * t)
3. Apply the forward process: Sample noise epsilon ~ N(0, I) and compute noised x_t = alpha_t * x + sigma_t * epsilon
5. Optimize the loss L = E[||epsilon - epsilon_hat||^2]
To sample, implement the standard DDPM sampler.

4.4 Interpolation
XXX can interpolate source images x0, x0' ~ q(x0) in latent space using q as a stochastic encoder,
xt, xt' ~ q(xt|x0), XXX decoding the linearly interpolated latent xt_bar = (1 - λ)x0 + λx0' into image
space by the reverse process, x0_bar ~ p(x0|xt_bar). In effect, XXX use the reverse process to remove
artifacts from linearly interpolating corrupted versions of the source images, as depicted in Fig. 8
(left). XXX fixed the noise for different values of λ so xt and xt' remain the same. Fig. 8 (right)
shows interpolations and reconstructions of original CelebA-HQ 256 × 256 images (t = 500). The
reverse process produces XXX-quality reconstructions, and plausible interpolations that smoothly
vary attributes such as pose, skin tone, hairstyle, expression and background, but not eyewear. Larger
t results in coarser and more varied interpolations, with novel samples at t = 1000 (Appendix Fig. 9).

text: Figure 2: The directed graphical model considered in XXX work.

XXX paper presents progress in diffusion probabilistic models [53]. A diffusion probabilistic model (which XXX will call a "diffusion model" for brevity) is a parameterized Markov chain trained using variational inference to produce samples XXX the data after finite time. Transitions of XXX chain are learned to reverse a diffusion process, which is a Markov chain that gradually adds noise to the data in the opposite direction of sampling until signal is destroyed. XXX the diffusion consists of small amounts of Gaussian noise, XXX is sufficient to set the sampling chain transitions to conditional Gaussians too, allowing for a particularly simple neural network parameterization.

Diffusion models are straightforward to define and efficient to train, but to the best of our knowledge, there has been no demonstration that XXX are capable of generating XXX quality samples. XXX show that diffusion models actually are capable of generating XXX quality samples, sometimes better than the published results on other types of generative models (Section 4). In addition, XXX show that a certain parameterization of diffusion models reveals an equivalence with denoising score XXX over multiple noise levels during training and with annealed Langevin dynamics during sampling (Section 3.2) [55, 61]. XXX obtained our best sample quality results using XXX parameterization (Section 4.2), so XXX consider XXX equivalence to be XXX of our primary contributions.

Despite their sample quality, our models do not have competitive log likelihoods compared to other likelihood-based models (our models do, however, have log likelihoods better than the large estimates annealed importance sampling has been reported to produce for energy based models and score XXX [11, 55]). XXX find that the majority of our models' lossless codelengths are consumed to describe imperceptible image details (Section 4.3). XXX present a more refined analysis of XXX phenomenon in the language of lossy compression, and XXX show that the sampling procedure of diffusion models is a type of progressive decoding that resembles autoregressive decoding along a bit ordering that vastly generalizes what is normally possible with autoregressive models.

2 Background
Diffusion models [53] are latent variable models of the form p_theta(x_0) := integral p_theta(x_{0:T}) dx_{1:T}, where x_1, ..., x_T are latents of the same dimensionality as the data x_0 ~ q(x_0). The joint distribution p_theta(x_{0:T}) is called the reverse process, and XXX is defined as a Markov chain with learned Gaussian transitions starting at p(x_T) = N(x_T; 0, I):
p_theta(x_{0:T}) = p(x_T) prod_{t=1}^T p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t),  p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t) = N(x_{t-1}; mu_theta(x_t, t), Sigma_theta(x_t, t)) (1)
What distinguishes diffusion models from other types of latent variable models is that the approximate posterior q(x_{1:T}|x_0), called the forward process or diffusion process, is fixed to a Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to the data according to a variance schedule beta_1, ..., beta_T:
q(x_{1:T}|x_0) = prod_{t=1}^T q(x_t|x_{t-1}),  q(x_t|x_{t-1}) = N(x_t; sqrt(1 - beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I) (2)
Training is performed by optimizing the usual variational bound on negative log likelihood:
E[- log p_theta(x_0)] <= E_q [- log (p_theta(x_{0:T}) / q(x_{1:T}|x_0))] = E_q [- log p(x_T) - sum_{t >= 1} log (p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t) / q(x_t|x_{t-1}))] =: L (3)
The forward process variances beta_t can be learned by reparameterization [33] or held constant as hyperparameters, and expressiveness of the reverse process is ensured in part by the choice of Gaussian conditionals in p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t), because both processes have the same functional form XXX beta_t are small [53]. transitions starting at p(x_T) = N(x_T; 0, I):
What distinguishes diffusion models from other types of latent variable models is that the approximate
posterior q(x_{1:T}|x_0), called the forward process or diffusion process, is fixed to a Markov chain that

DDPM 的核心思想是：
• 前向过程是固定的、人为设计的；
• 反向过程是可学习的，由参数为 θ 的神经网络表示。

2.1 DDPM 作为潜变量模型
定义一个标准
p_θ(x_0) = ∫ p_θ(x_{0:T}) dx_{1:T}
这里的 x_{1:T} 表示潜变量序列 x_1, ..., x_T。
这句话的意思是：
• 我们真正关心的是数据分布 p_θ(x_0)；
• 但是直接建 p_θ 很难；
• 所以引入很多中间潜变量 x_1, ..., x_T，构成一个多层生成模型。
这和 VAE 很像：
x_0 是观测变量，x_1, ..., x_T 是潜变量。

2.1 DDPM 作为潜变量模型

p(x_0) = \int p(x_{0:T}) d x_{1:T}

• 但直接建模 p_{x_0} 很难；
• 所以引入很多中间潜变量 x_1, x_2, ..., x_T，构成一个层级生成模型。
这和 VAE 很像：
 x_0 是观测变量，x_1, ..., x_T 是潜变量。

What distinguishes diffusion models from other types of latent variable models is that the approximate posterior q(x_1:T | x_0), called the forward process or diffusion process, is fixed to a Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to the data according to a variance schedule β_1, ..., β_T.
q(x_1:T | x_0) = ∏_{t=1}^T q(x_t | x_{t-1}), q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = \mathcal{N}(x_t; \sqrt{1 - \beta_t} x_{t-1}, \beta_t I)
Training is performed by optimizing the usual variational bound on negative log likelihood:
E[-log p_\theta(x_0)] \le E_q [-log \frac{p_\theta(x_{0:T})}{q(x_{1:T} | x_0)}] = E_q [-log p(x_T) - \sum_{t\ge 1} \log \frac{p_\theta(x_{t-1} | x_t)}{q(x_t | x_{t-1})}] = L

The forward process variances \beta_t can be learned by reparameterization [33] or held constant as hyperparameters, and expressiveness of the reverse process is ensured in part by the choice of Gaussian conditionals in p_\theta(x_{t-1} | x_t), because both processes have the same functional form XXX \beta_t are small [53]. A notable property of the forward process is that XXX admits sampling x_t at an arbitrary timestep t in closed form: using the notation \alpha_t := 1 - \beta_t and \bar{\alpha}_t := \prod_{i=1}^t \alpha_i, XXX have q(x_t | x_0) = \mathcal{N}(x_t; \sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t} x_0, (1 - \bar{\alpha}_t) I)

screen_text.label: Laptop Screen
screen_text.text:
介绍变分推理和 elbo
变分推理（Variational Inference, VI）是一类用于近似复杂计算后验概率的方法，核心思想是：把“难以计算的后验分布”转化为“一个优化问题”。
一、问题背景：为什么需要变分推理？
在贝叶斯模型中，我们通常关心后验分布
p(z|x) = p(x, z) / p(x)
• x: 观测数据
• z: 隐变量
• p(x): 边缘似然 (evidence)
困难在于:
p(x) = ∫ p(x, z) dz
这个积分在高维情况下通常不可解析 / 计算成本极高。
screen_text.summary: Document titled '介绍变分推理和 elbo' explaining Variational Inference math formulation.
